note: Regex accepted as unavoidable in tool code. Every row needs a written reason and an existing edge-case test file covering: empty input, no-match and boundary match, Unicode (multi-byte and astral), multiline, the anchors/quantifiers/lookarounds actually used, user-input escaping, a long input proving no catastrophic backtracking, and invalid caller-supplied patterns producing a named error. See docs/tools-campaign/CHARTER.md §7. Rows are keyed by file + the exact regex source (or `RegExp(...)` argument) and are checked by script/tools/verify-regex-policy.ts.

entries.reason: User-supplied pattern is the documented feature, not source parsing (charter §7.3): the caller's string is compiled as a RegExp source and matched against indexed symbol NAMES. It is validated before any index access (named InvalidRegexError), executed only inside the isolated scan worker, and bounded by REGEX_SCAN_CAP, PROJECTION_MAX and REGEX_TIME_BUDGET_MS, with every cut declared as truncated.

The worker compiles the SAME validated user pattern to run the bounded match loop; it is the isolation half of the regex-search feature (charter §7.3), not a parser. The allowlist pairs it with the edge-case suite that covers empty/anchored/Unicode/astral/multiline/escaping/invalid/long-input/catastrophic-backtracking patterns.
Framework-agnostic assertion-site probe for test-quality scoring; a framework's assert call has no AST node type this indexer exposes and includes() cannot express the optional `.word(` form.
Detects expect( sites across Jest/Vitest/Mocha/Chai; statement-level source evidence, no AST equivalence exists.
Chai should-style assertions are property accesses (should.equal) that only a pattern can recognise generically.
Matcher methods (toBe/toThrow/rejects...) appear after an arbitrary receiver expression, so the matcher method call itself is the only stable anchor.
Promise settlement evidence in assertions; two words with word boundaries, matched across any framework.
Error-path evidence: `try {` requires the brace as the next non-space token, which a plain includes('try') cannot enforce without false positives.
toThrow/throws are matcher/property names whose position cannot be found by string operations without reimplementing word boundaries.
Error-path evidence: `catch (` requires the call parenthesis, which includes('catch') cannot distinguish from the keyword followed by an identifier.
Data-driven test detection spans it.each/test.each/describe template literals/%s/$var; five alternative shapes with no common prefix.
Counts comment lines, which requires an alternation for line start, blank-prefix and three comment styles; character scanning would reimplement the same state machine.
Descriptive test names: a minimum name length inside quoted/backticked first argument, which needs the quote alternation and repetition counts.
Mock evidence: jest/sinon/vi fn/spyOn/mock plus mockImplementation and nock( across four frameworks; the alternatives share no prefix.
